report:
**Conclusion: Yes — the evidence supports that broad population mask-wearing reduces SARS-CoV-2 transmission and COVID-19 infections.**

Multiple lines of evidence converge on this conclusion:

1. **Systematic review (2025):** A systematic literature review found that masking policies and mask wearing are beneficial for preventing and reducing SARS-CoV-2 infections across various real-world settings. ([MDPI](https://www.mdpi.com/1660-4601/22/10/1590))

2. **PNAS population study (2022):** A study directly measuring mask wearing (not just mandates) found that population mask wearing notably reduced SARS-CoV-2 transmission, with mean mask-wearing levels corresponding to a ~19% decrease in transmission. ([PNAS](https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2119266119))

3. **Bangladesh randomized controlled trial:** The largest community mask RCT found that distributing and promoting masks increased proper mask use and reduced COVID-like illness, with surgical masks producing a statistically significant reduction. COVID-19 fell by 35% in people aged 60+ and 23% in those 50–60. ([The Conversation](https://theconversation.com/evidence-shows-that-yes-masks-prevent-covid-19-and-surgical-masks-are-the-way-to-go-167963); [EurekAlert](https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/936726))

4. **Cochrane review context:** The 2023 Cochrane update was widely misinterpreted as showing "masks don't work." Cochrane itself clarified that the review examined whether *interventions to promote mask wearing* slow respiratory virus spread, and results were inconclusive — not that masks themselves are ineffective. The review was limited to RCTs and did not capture the broader observational evidence. ([Cochrane statement](https://www.cochrane.org/about-us/news/statement-physical-interventions-interrupt-or-reduce-spread-respiratory-viruses-review); [FactCheck.org](https://www.factcheck.org/2023/03/scicheck-what-the-cochrane-review-says-about-masks-for-covid-19-and-what-it-doesnt/))

**Summary:** The overall body of evidence — including systematic reviews, a large RCT, and population-level observational studies — supports that widespread mask use reduces COVID-19 transmission, with stronger effects for surgical masks and among older populations.
